description:
On the /fly screen, the heliocentric transfer arc for some missions shows the correct start and end points (Earth at departure day, destination at arrival day) but sweeps the long way around the Sun (>180° of true anomaly) when the shorter path is physically correct. The arc either goes the long way CCW (>180°) or shows the correct sweep direction but with an internally consistent Keplerian ellipse whose eccentricity is a consequence of the fixed semi-major axis formula.

Expected: Every mission's outbound arc must sweep the shorter CCW true-anomaly path from Earth departure to destination arrival (≤180°). The arc must be a proper Keplerian ellipse with the Sun at one focus, must pass through both endpoints exactly, and must be monotonic and non-self-intersecting. The eccentricity and mid-point radius are consequences of the geometry, not independent correctness criteria.

Acceptance criteria:
- The arc sweeps ≤ 180° of true anomaly (the shorter CCW path) — verified for all 20 heliocentric missions. Currently FAILS for: galileo (243.9°), voyager-2 (313.3°), dawn (181.1°). The F2-selection heuristic must prefer the F2 candidate whose true-anomaly sweep is ≤ 180° when one exists. When both candidates produce sweeps > 180° (should not occur for complementary sweeps), pick the smaller sweep. When both are ≤ 180°, preserve the current behavior (pick closest to the heliocentric angle).
- The arc starts at p1 and ends at p2 within floating-point precision (1e-9 AU). All missions currently pass this.
- The arc is a proper Keplerian ellipse: every point satisfies r = a(1−e²)/(1+e·cos(ν)) for the same a and e (within floating-point precision). All missions currently pass this.
- The arc heliocentric angle is monotonic (always increasing CCW, no reversals). All missions currently pass this.
- The arc does not self-intersect. All missions currently pass this.
- The arc eccentricity is ≤ 0.95 (sanity check against near-parabolic rendering artifacts). Currently FAILS for: starship-mars-crew (e=0.9998). This is a secondary consequence of the semi-major axis formula a = (r1+r2)/2 being the Hohmann value, which is only correct for 180° angular separations. Fixing the F2 selection (criterion 1) is the primary required change; the a formula change is an independent design decision.

Domain facts:
- transferEllipse at src/lib/mission-arc.ts:144 computes a = (r1+r2)/2 (Hohmann baseline), then solves for F2 via circle intersection, then picks the F2 candidate with sweep closest to the heliocentric angle (desiredSweep).
- The two F2 candidates produce ellipses with complementary true-anomaly sweeps (θ and 2π−θ). The current heuristic picks the one closest to desiredSweep — but this selects the long arc (θ > 180°) when desiredSweep > 180°.
- The desiredSweep at line 173-175 is the raw CCW heliocentric angle from p1 to p2, normalized to [0, 2π). It can exceed 180° (e.g., 243.9° for galileo, 313.3° for voyager-2).
- The fix is localized to the F2 selection loop at lines 181-193: replace the distance-to-desiredSweep heuristic with a preference for the candidate whose sweep ≤ 180°.
- The semi-major axis formula a = (r1+r2)/2 is a separate design choice (Hohmann baseline). The bulge for near-conjunction Mars missions (e.g., hope-probe mid-r 2.15 AU vs 1.26 AU Hohmann mean) is a consequence of this formula, not a bug in the F2 selection. If the eccentricity > 0.95 (starship-mars-crew) is unacceptable, the a formula must be revisited as an independent change.
